sources.name: OpenSSF CVE Benchmark
sources.notes: Current public main-branch inventory inspected for this catalog has 223 CVE JSON manifests. Each records an upstream repository and pre-patch/post-patch commits; screen the source language and reproduce in isolation before promoting any entry.

sources.name: SecBench.js
sources.license: No repository SPDX license declared; obtain/verify reuse permission before copying benchmark files.
sources.notes: Public repository documents 600 reported npm vulnerabilities with test payloads and per-case package metadata. Its JavaScript focus makes it a pattern and runtime-oracle source for TypeScript adaptations, not evidence that an adaptation is valid.

sources.name: GitHub Advisory Database
sources.available_cases: Living npm advisory corpus; no fixed count asserted in this catalog.
sources.notes: GitHub-reviewed advisory records are published in OSV format and carry GHSA IDs, affected package/version data, and references when available. Select only advisory records with a repository and review the provenance and affected range before case construction.

sources.name: CVEfixes
sources.available_cases: 12,107 fixing commits; 11,873 CVEs; 4,249 projects (v1.0.8, all languages)
sources.notes: Relational data covers repository, commit, file, and function levels. It is a broad discovery source rather than a TypeScript-labelled benchmark; filter and independently resolve upstream revisions.

sources.name: TS-VulBench
sources.license: Not stated on the public landing page; dataset download requires IEEE DataPort subscription.
sources.notes: Landing page describes 100 independently constructed TypeScript files with one intentionally introduced weakness each. No sample IDs are recorded because the public page gates the archive; do not treat it as locally available.

sources.name: SecJS
sources.license: Apache-2.0 for framework code; upstream snapshots retain their own licenses.
sources.available_cases: No packaged ArenaJS dataset currently committed.
sources.notes: Public artifact provides a collection/construction pipeline and an evaluation harness, but explicitly does not ship the generated dataset files. Treat as a reproducible-discovery pipeline, not an immediately reusable case set.

sources.name: CVE List V5
sources.available_cases: Live official CVE catalogue; no TypeScript-specific count asserted.
sources.notes: Use as the official CVE-record cross-reference. Consumers must inspect both the CNA and CVE Program containers when present, then resolve the upstream source and patch separately.
